records.quote: In general. you can duduce the law of the coordinate of the midpoint
records.text: In general, you can deduce the law of the coordinate of the midpoint of a straight segment as follows.

records.quote: If A (x1, y1), B (x2, y2), M (x, y) where M in the midpoint
records.claim: If A(x1,y1), B(x2,y2), M(x,y) where M is the midpoint of AB, then triangles BEM and MDA are congruent, so AD = ME. Hence x − x1 = x2 − x, so 2x = x1 + x2, x = (x1+x2)/2. Similarly MD = BE gives y − y1 = y2 − y, so 2y = y1 + y2, y = (y1+y2)/2. So M((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2).
records.notes: Printed as a derivation; 'cogruent' misspelt as 'cogruent'/'cogruent' in print.

records.quote: (x2 ;y2) B (x;y) M (x1 ;y1) A
records.caption: Coordinate axes x'x and y'y meeting at F. Points A(x1;y1), M(x;y), B(x2;y2) on a slanted segment AB with tick marks on AM and MB. Right triangles: D below M with AD labelled x − x1, DM labelled y − y1; E below B with ME's horizontal side labelled x2 − x, BE labelled y2 − y. Triangles AMD and MBE shaded.

records.label: Example
records.quote: If C is the midpoint of AB and A (3, - 7) , B (- 5, - 3)
records.stem: If C is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$ and A(3, -7), B(-5, -3).
solution: Then the coordinates of midpoint of AB are $\left(\frac{3-5}{2},\frac{-7-3}{2}\right)$ i.e. $(-1,-5)$

records.label: Example
records.quote: A B C D is a parallorgram, A (3, 2), B (4, -5), C (0- 3)
records.stem: A B C D is a parallorgram, A (3, 2), B (4, -5), C (0- 3) - Find the two coordinates of the point at which the two diagonals intersect. Then find the coordinates of point D.
solution: The figure A B C D is a parallelogram, M is the intersection point of its diagonal.
∴ The coordinates of the point D are (-1, 4)
